data.title: Cellectis falls as Citizens downgrades on pivot to genetic medicines
data.description:
Cellectis (CLLS) ADRs continued to drop for the second straight session on Tuesday as Citizens Capital Markets downgraded the French biotech, citing its decision to prioritize its in vivo gene editing therapies over CAR-T cell therapies.

The Paris-based company traded sharply lower on Monday after unveiling a strategic transformation to focus on its in vivo gene editing candidates, HEAL-101 and HEAL-201, targeted at cardiovascular diseases.

Concurrently, the company announced plans to discontinue the development of CAR-T cell therapies lasme-cel and eti-cel, a decision that could delay related clinical catalysts to late 2027/2028, according to Citizens Analyst Silvan Turkcan.

"We are bullish on genetic medicines for CVD and believe CLLS may provide a unique approach, but clinical catalysts have been pushed back to late 2027/2028, and early biomarkers may not be very helpful in de-risking a program," wrote Turkcan.

With Cellectis (CLLS) shares trading at roughly a 28% discount to its $169M worth of cash reserves, the analyst argued the company is fairly valued in line with its biotech peers encountering similar uncertainties. Turkcan downgraded the stock to Market Perform from Market Outperform.

data.title: Two Robinhood employees charged with fraud over misappropriating insider information
data.description:
U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York, charged two Robinhood (HOOD) (HOOD:CA) employees with fraud.

Robinhood engineers Hefu Chai and Huaisong Xiang were charged with commodities fraud and wire fraud arising from a scheme to misappropriate confidential business information from their employer.

The information was allegedly used to trade perpetual futures on the decentralized derivatives exchange, Hyperliquid.

According to the complaint filed in the Manhattan federal court, Chai and Xiang had access to nonpublic information related to whether and when Robinhood will support additional cryptocurrencies for trading on a subsidiary digital asset trading platform.

"Today's charges make clear that corporate insiders cannot evade the securities and commodities laws by trading based on misappropriated information in derivatives like perpetual futures, tokenized securities, or other similar financial instruments," said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.

data.title: BHP Port Hedland workers to seek arbitration in labor dispute, union says
data.description:
Workers at BHP's (BHP) ‌Port Hedland facility in Australia will pursue arbitration after the two sides failed to reach terms on a new wage deal, the Combined BHP Ports Unions said Tuesday, according to Reuters.

The union, which represents ~450 operators and maintenance workers at Port Hedland, will apply for an intractable bargaining declaration, which ​allows Australia's Fair Work Commission to set terms for ⁠the ⁠agreement.

BHP (BHP) has offered ​a 17% pay increase for most workers over the four years of the ​agreement, which ⁠will include a A$25K transition payment over two years, as well as an increase to roster allowances, but the union argues that ~40% of the workforce would be worse off under the company's proposal.

BHP (BHP) is "unwilling to negotiate an agreement that reflects the specialized skills, extreme conditions and significant ‌personal sacrifices ⁠of the people who generated the company more than $13 billion in profit this year," the union said in a statement.

Port Hedland is the world's ⁠largest ⁠iron ore export hub and the main shipping gateway for ​BHP's (BHP) Pilbara operations.

data.title: General Motors' CFO expects Q4 to be seasonally weaker
data.description:
General Motors (GM) management said that as a result of 35K fewer trucks delivered during the next generation pickup changeover, the fourth quarter of 2026 is expected to be "seasonally weaker" than the second and third quarters of this year.

Speaking at the Morgan Stanley 14th Annual Laguna Conference, chief financial officer Paul Jacobson remarked that if things don’t get out of balance, “Fourth quarter is typically seasonally weaker than Q2 and Q3 this year…seasonally less than 35K units is about the right way to think about Q4." 

Jacobson also noted that 2027 is “going to be a bit of a flat spot” for EVs.

“EV profitability has been hit really hard over the last couple of years. First, tariffs; second, everybody was logging EV credits as part of the variable profit equation…both of those went the wrong direction against profitability.”

The company still believes EVs are a long-term play, “but we’ve got to get them profitable,” something Jacobson believes GM is outperforming its rivals on.

data.title: Midday Need to Know: RTX sees defense demand, Empire State Manufacturing slows & more
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages declined Tuesday as Treasury yields remained the focal point and investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decision later this week.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last -0.7%.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

Treasury Secretary Bessent forecasts fiscal consolidation: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent  told the House Financial Services Committee that the federal deficit-to-GDP ratio declined to 5.7%-5.8% for fiscal year 2026, down from approximately 6.3% inherited from the prior administration. Bessent said fiscal contraction would have continued but for tariff refunds and confirmed that additional fiscal consolidation is forthcoming. He also addressed AI regulation, stating that creators of advanced AI models should bear legal responsibility for safety rather than receiving "a blank check on liability."

Empire State manufacturing growth cools in September: The New York Fed's Empire State Manufacturing Index  fell to 7.6 in September from 20.6 in August, missing the 14.1 consensus. While the headline figure remained in positive territory, new orders slowed sharply to 2.0 from 17.3 and shipments turned negative at -3.2. Pricing pressures intensified, with prices paid rising to 63.1 from 58.6 and prices received climbing to 28.1 from 22.7. Employment grew at a solid pace, with the number of employees index edging up to 10.6 from 9.3.

RTX projects durable growth on defense backlog and air travel: RTX (RTX) Chairman and CEO Chris Calio  told Morgan Stanley's annual Laguna Conference that the aerospace and defense company holds a backlog of approximately $289 billion, excluding five major munitions framework agreements and a recently awarded seven-year, $23 billion Tomahawk contract. Calio projected medium-term operating margins of 19%-20% for Collins Aerospace and 2026 free cash flow of about $8.6 billion. About 48% of Raytheon's backlog is international, up four percentage points from a year earlier, as geopolitical tensions drive increased defense spending globally.

FDA launches pilot to accelerate drug clinical trial approvals: The U.S. FDA  announced the Expedited IND Pilot Program under HHS' Operation TrialBlazer, designed to shorten the time from drug identification to first-in-human trials. The initiative allows rolling component reviews with qualified research institutions rather than waiting for all application components before review begins. The FDA noted that U.S. first-in-human trials currently take up to two years, considerably slower than in China and Australia. Applications are being accepted through Oct. 30, with the agency expecting to select eight to 10 sponsor-institution pairs.

data.title: Target sets its fall sales event for the same days as Amazon's
data.description:
Target Corporation (TGT) announced on Tuesday that its fall Target Circle Deal Days event will run October 6–7 in a direct challenge to Amazon's (AMZN) Prime Big Deal Days shopping event. The retailer will offer Target Circle members up to 40% off thousands of products. The promotion spans fall apparel, home décor, kitchen tools, beauty, toys, technology, and early holiday merchandise. As a perk, Target Circle 360 members can begin shopping select offers on October 5.

The Minneapolis-based company's strategy is focused on budget-conscious seasonal shopping, such as replacing summer clothing, refreshing homes for fall, and starting holiday gift purchases early. Promoted offers include 40% off select family apparel and outdoor holiday décor, 30% off selected Threshold furniture and Hearth & Hand with Magnolia products, discounts on select Dyson vacuums, and savings of up to 40% on toys, laptops, and other tech. Target (TGT) also aims to use the event to recruit and deepen loyalty membership.

The annual fall sales event evolved from Target Circle Week, a longer loyalty-sale format. In fall 2025, Target held a seven-day Circle Week from October 5–11, featuring discounts of up to 50% and daily deals.

Shares of Target (TGT) were down 2.0% in Tuesday afternoon trading.

data.title: Scholar Rock downgraded at Barclays despite FDA approval of SMA therapy
data.description:
Scholar Rock (SRRK) shares continued to tumble on Tuesday as Barclays downgraded the Massachusetts-area biotech despite last week’s FDA approval of its lead asset, Isembyld, for spinal muscular atrophy, a rare neuromuscular disorder.

Despite a 7% YTD gain, Scholar Rock (SRRK) has lost more than 14% since Friday, when the company became a commercial-stage biotech following the FDA nod for Isembyld as a late-line option for those aged two years and older with SMA.  

However, Barclays analyst Etzer Darout cut his rating on SRRK to Equal Weight from Overweight, citing a more balanced risk-reward setup post-approval and indicating a cautious tone on the company’s non-SMA pipeline.

“While we continue to view these programs as important sources of long-term optionality, our valuation today remains driven primarily by the SMA opportunity. We believe additional clinical validation will likely be required before we can ascribe meaningful incremental value to the broader pipeline beyond SMA,” Darout wrote.

The analyst argued that future upside to his above-consensus estimates will increasingly depend on a commercial execution that could surpass his expectations and the company’s pipeline expansion opportunities beyond SMA.

However, Darout raised his price target on Scholar Rock (SRRK) to $58 from $55 per share, noting that the pricing the management announced for Isembyld on Monday slightly exceeded his prior estimates.

data.title: Transocean jumps after securing $80M ultra-deepwater rig contract
data.description:
Transocean (RIG) rises 8.6% in Tuesday's trading after saying its Deepwater Conqueror ultra-deepwater drillship was awarded a two-well contract for work in Equatorial Guinea by an undisclosed operator.

The company said the estimated 170-day campaign is expected to begin in 2027 in direct continuation of the rig's current contract in the U.S. Gulf and contribute ~$80M in backlog, excluding additional services and compensation for mobilization and demobilization.

Transocean (RIG) owns or has partial ownership interests in and operates a fleet of 27 mobile offshore drilling units, consisting of 20 ultra-deepwater floaters and seven harsh environment floaters.

The company said in August that Africa would drive demand for new deepwater contracts, with the gain expected to offset a decline in U.S. Gulf-based contracts.

data.title: Trump out-traded all members of Congress combined - report
data.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump and his wealth managers executed nearly 28.7K security transactions in the 17 months following his second inauguration—outpacing all members of Congress combined—even as he pushes legislation banning lawmakers from buying stocks, according to a media report Tuesday.

During that same period, Capitol Hill lawmakers collectively reported about 22.2K similar transactions, Bloomberg reported, citing security transaction disclosure forms.

The contrast marks a notable shift from his first term, when Trump's financial disclosures contained mostly illiquid real estate holdings and other privately held ventures. His portfolio now spans thousands of holdings in stocks (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ), bonds (TLT) (SHY) and cryptocurrencies (IBIT) (ETHA).

The stock-purchasing ban passed by House Republicans in July exclusively restricts members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children. The legislation leaves the presidency untouched—even though the commander-in-chief has singularly wide-ranging access to U.S. intelligence and the power to influence entire sectors with an executive order or social media post.

Backing the proposed House measure, Trump had stated in his recent State of the Union address that it must be enacted "without delay" so that members of Congress "cannot corruptly profit from using insider information." He remains the only U.S. president this century to disclose active trading of individual stocks, continuing transactions that would be prohibited for lawmakers under the very legislation he champions.

In June alone, Trump made more than 1K securities trades, including significant purchases of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B), Visa (V), Mastercard (MA), Palantir (PLTR) and Cintas (CTAS), financial disclosure published by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics. The largest transaction was a June 22 sale of between $5M and $25M of shares in the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation Index Fund ETF (VIG).
